title: Hosted SSE inflight-offset reconciler and customer-visible duplication mitigation
creator: Lena Ortiz
description: Several enterprise customers reported duplicated partial tokens and truncated final outputs after reconnecting to hosted SSE streams. Incidents were seen across sessions that experienced network flaps or intermediate proxy resets. The client-visible symptom: when a client reconnects within 30s, the new stream sometimes repeats the last N tokens and occasionally omits the true finalization marker, producing inconsistent transcripts and failed end-of-stream semantics. This ticket scopes detection, reconciliation, and a minimal compatibility change to server-client handshake to prevent duplicates while preserving low-latency resumption.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Start a hosted SSE chat generation with a customer-sized prompt (600-1200 tokens).
2) Force a mid-generation TCP/HTTP/Proxy disconnect (simulate ephemeral NAT churn).
3) Reconnect using the same session token within 10s and resume polling for SSE chunks.
4) Observe duplicated trailing tokens in the resumed stream and sometimes missing final delimiter event.
impact: Multiple paying customers observed truncated or duplicated outputs leading to incorrect user-facing responses and support escalations. Some customers switched traffic to dedicated endpoints as a short-term mitigation.
telemetry_summary: Frequency: ~0.03% of streamed sessions in prod region us-west-2 over the last 7 days. Spike correlated with an edge proxy rollout between 2025-01-12 and 2025-01-15. A/B logging shows repeated sequence IDs with overlapping offsets in ~80% of affected sessions.
root_cause: We relied on last-seen client offset stored only in ephemeral connection memory during streaming. After disconnects, the resumed handshake lacked a monotonic inflight-offset verification and the server accepted overlapping token windows from the backlog buffer, emitting duplicates. The edge proxy's FIN reordering exacerbated the issue by causing server to believe tail fragments were acknowledged when they were not.
fix_details: 1) Introduce X-Redwood-Stream-Offset header: client attaches last-consumed token-offset when reconnecting. Server validates offset against durable session checkpoint (lightweight Redis entry keyed by session id). 2) Add chunk-level checksum and monotonic sequence anchor per event to detect overlaps server-side; reject or truncate overlapping token ranges. 3) Compatibility shim: if client does not send X-Redwood-Stream-Offset, server falls back to best-effort old behavior but emits a warning metric and increments compat counter. 4) Persist finalization sentinel to durable checkpoint on final flush to prevent missing end-of-stream on quick disconnect. 5) Add server-side reconciler that merges overlapping fragments deterministically (prefer first-seen tokens and drop duplicates).
tests: Unit tests for header parsing, checksum verification, and reconciler logic. Integration tests using proxy-chaos harness that simulates FIN reordering and reconnects. End-to-end tests against our hosted stack with a synthetic load of 10k short/long sessions validating no duplicates and correct finalization. Add regression alerts for duplicate-token-rate > 0.01%.
rollback_plan: Feature is gated behind a runtime flag 'inflight-offset-reconciler'. Rollback by toggling feature flag to false and redeploying the config. If Redis checkpointing causes an outage, revert to in-memory path by disabling the gate; plan includes a one-hour maintenance window and tracked customer communication template.
deployment_plan: Canary deploy reconciler to 5% of traffic in us-west-2 with verbose metrics. Monitor duplicate-token-rate, finalization-miss-rate, and reconnect-latency. After 24h with no regression, increase to 25%, then 100% across hosted regions. Dedicated/private customers get opt-in patch release and a migration guide for on-prem Redis requirement or in-process small KV fallback.
monitoring: duplicate-token-rate - histogram by region and model
compat-fallback-count - track clients not sending offset header
comments: 2025-01-18 - Lena Ortiz: Ticket opened after urgent customer call. Collected network captures and initial Grafana query results. Assigned to Ravi for triage.
2025-01-20 - Ravi Patel: Confirmed reproducer with local proxy that reorders FIN frames. Proposed introducing monotonic offset header and durable checkpoint. Posted initial design in Confluence.
2025-01-23 - Mei Chen (SRE): Raised concern about Redis latency at scale; suggested a small memory-backed LRU fallback per server core for very short lived sessions.
2025-01-26 - Design review: Added backwards-compatible header and metric to avoid breaking older SDKs. Decided against changing SSE framing for now to keep SDK changes minimal.
2025-01-30 - QA: Integration tests passing in staging. Added chaos tests for proxy FIN reordering. Noted a minor perf cost on resume path ~0.6ms median.
2025-02-01 - PM (Anika Rao): Customer-facing mitigation sent; recommended coordinated release with dedicated account managers. Preparing postmortem doc.
2025-02-02 - Ravi Patel: Submitted PRs for runtime and edge. Running canary rollout in us-west-2 5% now; metrics look good so far.
resolution: Under review pending final QA sign-off; canary shows duplicate-token-rate dropped to 0.0008% and finalization-miss-rate to near-zero in the canary cohort. Backwards compatibility observed for older SDKs with increased compat-fallback-count metrics.
postmortem: Root cause is a combination of edge proxy FIN reordering and absence of a durable, monotonic resume offset. Fix introduced reconciliation via durable checkpoints and a handshake header to make resumption deterministic. Operationally, add an alert for rising duplicate-token-rate and include SSE resume behavior in onboarding docs for customers. Plan to document the header in SDK release notes and provide migration tests for Private customers before enabling by default.
